newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mercer says he leaves ANZ in good shape.
newsitem.headline: Mercer says he leaves ANZ in good shape.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand Group Ltd (ANZ) chief executive officer Don Mercer said on Wednesday on announcing his retirement that it was time to hand the bank to fresh blood to take it into a new era.

Mercer's surprise annoucement after almost five years in the top job with the Melbourne-based bank followed the release of ANZ's record half year net profit, which was in stark contrast to the first set of results over which Mercer presided.
ANZ reported an 18 percent rise in net profit to A$615 million in the six months ended March 31, 1997.
Mercer was only six weeks into the job when ANZ posted a A$579 million loss for the year to September 30, 1992, the first loss in living memory for the bank.

The Scotish-born banker took over ANZ in October 1992, when the bank was suffering from the recession of the early 1990s and writing off loans to failed property developers from the credit binge of the late 1980s.

"In my period...it has been period of stabilising the organisation and of regaining the momentum of it and then transforming it to what you see today, which is an extraordinary well performing organisation," Mercer told reporters.

Under Mercer reign, the ANZ share price has risen nearly 250 percent and closed at a record A$8.75 on Wednesday, giving a market value of just over A$13 billion following the better than expected half year result.
However, some bank analysts said Mercer had not entirely turned the bank around.
"Where he seems to have failed is to reduce costs," said one Sydney-based banking analyst.
ANZ's cost to income ratio improved to 63.9 percent in the 1996/97 half, down from 66.1 percent a year earlier.
However, this was still seen at the higher end of the cost scale for Australia's four major banks.
"But I think he has done very well giving the disaster there was when he took it over," the analyst said.
Mercer, 56, said he had no plans after his retirement from the bank. He was also coy on who would filling his shoes when he has gone.
"I think we should be quietly putting the new team in place rather then getting someone that is not of their making," said Mercer.
Analysts said one candidate for Mercer's position could be former Bank of Melbourne Ltd managing director David Airey, who joined ANZ earlier this year to manage their New Zealand operations.
